items.actClause: AN ACT to establish a report on arts and music education in elementary and secondary schools; and providing for the repeal of such provisions upon expiration thereof
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S1428

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to establish a report on arts and music education in elementary
and secondary schools; and providing for the repeal of such provisions
upon expiration thereof

 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :

To establish a report on arts and music education in elementary and
secondary schools for students and make recommendations on the
curriculum and time spent on arts and music education

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :

Section 1: The NYS Commissioner of Education is required to create a
procedure in which school districts report to the State Education
Department on compliance with current arts instruction requirements
including visual arts, music, dance and theater as required by law and
regulation in elementary and secondary public schools. This is a
onetime requirement so that SED can prepare its report on music and
arts education. The commissioner shall report to the Governor and
Legislature on or before July 1, 2018 regarding the findings.

Section 2: Establishes the effective date.

 JUSTIFICATION :

Based on data reports from the New York City Department of Education,
art programs diminish as students get older. About 90% of elementary
school students have access to at least three of the four art
disciplines (visual arts, music, dance, and theater), while 50% of
middle and only about 30% of high school students have the same access
available. These reduced levels of art in the upper grades means less
variety for older students, and therefore fewer reasons or motivations
to participate in such arts programs and in other school activities in
general.

Current research demonstrates that integrating the arts into general
education throughout the learning process, significantly enhances
students' cognitive, personal, and social abilities. Quality arts
education is central to a complete education and it is required by
state law.

The arts promote the health and well-being of children, including
academic and personal growth, critical thinking and analytical skills,
and the motivation to stay in school and excel by encouraging
expression, creativity, innovative thinking, and cooperative learning
experiences. A quality arts education is a proven tool to open doors
of opportunity through the development of analytical and
problem-solving skills that are indispensable in the 21st century
workforce.

Arts in Education programs have long been valued learning experiences
in New York State schools. The State's arts and cultural institutions,
including museums, libraries, historical sites, performing arts
companies, and teaching artists are crucial in supporting and
enriching New York's school curriculum. Studies by the Guggenheim
Museum, National Art Education Association, and The Center for Arts
Education have proven that students who are engaged in the arts
develop a more complete understanding of personal identity,
appreciation for culture, and connection with community. Furthermore,
art education creates an environment where excitement, possibility,
discovery, and imagination can thrive. Studies also indicate that art
education can have a profound effect on students with special needs.
They are able to build confidence, develop social and motor skills, as
well as become more self-aware. The difference art can make in the
life of a special needs child is immeasurable, and for this reason
should be championed at every opportunity.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

2015-16: S.1148-A/A.3525-B (Titone)
2014: S.7242/A.8763-A (Titone)

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect immediately, and shall expire and be deemed
repealed January 1, 2020 or on the one hundred and eightieth day after
the report required by subdivisions two and three of section one of
this act is submitted to the governor, the temporary president of the
senate, the speaker of the Assembly, and the chairs of the senate and
assembly committees on education, whichever shall be later; provided,
further, that the state education department shall notify the
legislative bill drafting commission upon the submission of the report
required by subdivisions two and three of section one of this act to
the governor, the temporary president of the senate, the speaker of
the assembly, and the chair of the senate and assembly committees on
education, in order that the commission may maintain an accurate and
timely effective data base of the official text of the laws of the
state of New York in furtherance of effectuating the provisions of
section 44 of the legislative law and section 70-b of the public
officers law.

summary: Establishes report on arts and music education in elementary and secondary schools to study and make recommendations on the curriculum and time spent on arts and music education.
